hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap with nine road widening projects unfunded
hero.teaser: Martin County will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years but only $701 million is currently available, leaving nine identified road widening projects without funding.
hero.body:
Martin County faces a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next two decades, with nine road widening projects left without financial backing, according to a PowerPoint obtained through a public records request. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years, but only $701 million is currently available. This means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified transportation needs.

Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said the cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources. The significant funding gap has forced difficult decisions about which transportation projects can move forward and which must remain on hold.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708.

State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities due to safety concerns. Beltran said fatal crashes as well as serious injury crashes were just enormous on that corridor, with improvements estimated at about $300 million. The substantial price tag for State Road 710 alone represents nearly half of the total funding shortfall and highlights the challenge facing county officials as they balance safety needs against available resources. The funding gap affects not just road widening projects but a range of transportation improvements needed across the county over the next two decades.

cards.headline: Second arrest made in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher on Essex Drive
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced Tuesday that a second person has been arrested in the fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes, 66. Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death. Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. Deputies said the fatal shooting was premeditated.

The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Karen Moye was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, told detectives immediately after the shooting that the pair did not have a good relationship and that Mincey told her he was expressing fear in the days leading up to the shooting, the arrest affidavit said. Moye told detectives Mincey said Barnes was trying to kill him and Mincey did not want to be left alone at the house.

Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Tuesday during a press conference that detectives uncovered information indicating that Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to the homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms. In a follow-up interview with Moye on Monday, she gave a detective conflicting accounts of what happened on the day of the shooting, according to an arrest affidavit. She told detectives she was in fear of Barnes and that something might happen between Mincey and Barnes. When asked why she didn't notify police, she said she thought both of them would get in trouble.

Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children. Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as a pillar of the community and father figure. Deputies said the fatal shooting remains an active investigation and are encouraging anyone with information to contact the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County commissioners deny private Christian school proposal in Jupiter Farms
cards.body:
Palm Beach County commissioners voted Tuesday to deny a controversial proposal to build a large private Christian school in Jupiter Farms after hours of emotional public debate over traffic, growth and the future of the community's rural character. The proposal from Calvary Church would have brought a K-12 private Christian school to a vacant site on Indiantown Road, with plans for nearly 1,000 students. Palm Beach County Mayor Sara Baxter was the only commissioner to vote in favor of the project, citing the need for private Christian education in the area.

For more than three hours, residents lined up to speak, with traffic emerging as one of the most contentious topics of the night. Opponents warned the project was simply too large for Jupiter Farms and would fundamentally change the character of the community. One speaker told commissioners that preserving the rural residential and equestrian character of Jupiter is the objective of county plans, noting the scale of the proposed school is larger than the proposed Home Depot and has more customers in it. Supporters pushed back, with one resident saying fewer buses would result and envisioning grandchildren riding bikes to school, adding it would be much safer for the kids.

Commissioners spent significant time questioning details presented by county staff and project representatives. One issue centered on concerns from the zoning board that development would cover roughly 80 percent of the property. Project officials disputed that interpretation, explaining that required buffer landscaping between the school and nearby homes was being counted as development, along with a planned lake on the site. Another major point of disagreement involved whether there is actually a need for another school in the area. Calvary representatives argued nearby schools are already at capacity, but commissioners noted many schools highlighted in the presentation were public schools while the proposed project would be a private school with tuition costs and different enrollment requirements that would not benefit public school students. Commissioner Joel Flores pointed to where public support was coming from during the hearing, saying only about 25 percent of those who spoke in favor of the project were from Jupiter, while many supporters came from outside the area, including Port St. Lucie and Boca Raton.

The county's Zoning Commission Board voted unanimously last month to recommend denial of the proposal. Calvary Church officials say they have not decided what comes next. Church leaders say it remains unclear whether they will rework the project and try again or move forward with selling the property instead. The county denied the application without prejudice, which means the school project could be brought back in a different form, but Calvary officials would have to go through the same administrative process.

cards.headline: Man Killed Fleeing ICE Agents on Florida Highway as Agency Faces Scrutiny Over Fatal Encounters
cards.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was struck by a semi trailer truck while fleeing from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents on State Road 16 near a gas station in Florida. The man was one of four people who fled on foot during an encounter with ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents in the parking lot of a local gas station and convenience store. Florida Highway Patrol officials confirmed they were not involved in the incident but have opened an investigation into the death. According to the state highway patrol, the man ran across State Road 16 and into the path of the tractor trailer. He was struck in the right lane and sustained fatal injuries on scene.

Details about the victim, including his name, nationality and immigration status, were not immediately available. ICE and the Department of Homeland Security have not yet commented on the incident. The state highway patrol said in a statement to Scripps News that during the encounter, four occupants of a vehicle fled on foot, with one running across the highway and into the path of the oncoming truck.

The death comes as ICE is under increasing scrutiny for multiple fatal encounters nationwide. Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man living in Maine, was fatally shot by ICE agents Monday during a traffic stop. Senator Angus King said Guerrero was not the target of an immigration operation. Days earlier, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally wounded during a traffic stop involving ICE in Houston. Like the shooting in Maine, Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was trying to find.

The Trump administration ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to pause most traffic stops on Tuesday following the fatal incidents. Florida Highway Patrol officials have confirmed their investigation into the State Road 16 death remains ongoing. The incident marks the latest in a series of deadly encounters involving ICE agents that have drawn attention to the agency's enforcement tactics. The pause on traffic stops comes as federal immigration enforcement operations continue under increased public and political scrutiny.

cards.headline: Florida gas prices jump about 20 cents a gallon amid Strait of Hormuz military tensions
cards.teaser: Florida gas prices rose about 20 cents a gallon Tuesday, catching many drivers off guard as military activity in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil and wholesale gasoline prices higher.
cards.body:
Patrick DeHaan, a petroleum analyst with GasBuddy, said the spike is part of a broader regional trend. We're seeing Florida along with other states getting engaged in the price cycling jump, he said. DeHaan said the increases came in direct response to developments overseas. That's because oil prices jumped yesterday as did the wholesale price of gasoline, he said. He said those moves were driven by the latest military activity in the Strait of Hormuz.

Jalisse Thomas, who was filling up her car in West Palm Beach, said the constant fluctuation is a financial strain. It doesn't go down fast enough, and money doesn't go up up either, so it is hard, Thomas said. DeHaan said prices do move in both directions, but the sharp increases simply draw more attention than gradual declines. It's a lot easier to notice a one day 30 cent increase then it is to notice a nickel every day, that nickel everyday doesn't add up at the same pace that a 30-cent jump does, he said. DeHaan pointed to a recent example, noting that from May 20 to June 20 of this year, gas prices dropped a dollar a gallon.

cards.headline: Atlanta increases security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal Wednesday
cards.teaser: Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta after videos showed fans clashing in Miami.
cards.body:
Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War.

Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend. Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is the first time since 1966 that England's national team has earned a berth in the semifinals.

Argentina has claimed three World Cup titles and has been the tournament's runner-up twice. The winner of Wednesday's semifinal will face Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Council votes to rezone lot behind couple's home from residential to commercial
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie couple is searching for answers after the city council voted unanimously to rezone the lot behind their home from residential to commercial, despite their months-long opposition.
cards.body:
Margaret and Joseph Mucciolo have called Port St. Lucie home for years, drawn to the property by the beautiful setting and views of nature. Margaret Mucciolo said the setting is what pushed them to purchase the property. But now they say their little piece of paradise is under threat after the Port St. Lucie City Council approved changing the lot behind their yard, where trees currently stand, to be rezoned from residential to commercial.

The council says the change is necessary to reduce traffic in the neighborhood. Adding commercial closer to our neighborhoods reduces the length of trips, said one council member. Which reduces overall traffic because if you have commercial closer to you, your trips are shorter and it reduces the burden on the overall network. The Mucciolos fought the rezoning for months and spoke at Monday's meeting, voicing their concerns. Joseph Mucciolo said it seems like except for the news media, nothing has been done to address their opposition.

The council held its second reading Monday. While there was public comment, it was what's called a quasi-judicial hearing, meaning council members act as a panel of judges, applying existing zoning rules to a specific property and making decisions based strictly on sworn testimony and factual evidence, not public opinion. The Mucciolos say they will be exploring any kind of appeal process to change this outcome or to change the next one.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound couple seeks community support as husband battles head and neck cancer
cards.teaser: Dave and Faren Motz of Hobe Sound are asking for community support as they navigate a cancer diagnosis that has cost the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket.
cards.body:
The couple moved to Hobe Sound and purchased a property, but just months after settling in, Dave was diagnosed with head and neck cancer. As the couple searched for the right healthcare in Florida, AdventHealth in Celebration provided programs and grants that became a critical resource. Dave underwent nearly seven weeks of daily radiation treatments. The repeated visits to Orlando, biopsies, scans, and exams added up, costing the couple nearly $20,000 out of pocket. Their age and income kept them from qualifying for Medicare or Medicaid. Faren said some days were good and other days were not during the treatment period. Doctors told Dave he has an 85% chance of recovery.

Dave, a former firefighter, had long been the family's provider. Now, Faren has stepped up to support them both. Dave said Faren got him through the surgery, toughed it out, and drove him back and forth from Orlando. Through it all, the couple has leaned on their faith. Dave said he was glad it was him and not her because to see her go through it would have been heartbreaking. Faren said she keeps telling him all the time how glad she is he's here. Faren works at Latitudes at the Jupiter Beach Resort, where those who want to show their support can stop by and visit. Those who would like to contribute financially can donate to the family's GoFundMe at Standing with Dave Motz in his cancer battle.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce neighbors pack planning meeting over Causeway Cove high-rise development proposal
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project on Monday as neighbors packed the chamber. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space. The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing.

Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will change the character of the area. "We're going to put this big old conglomerate up here, and I'm just afraid it's going to take away from the beauty of this place," Brewster said. Dennis Fein attended the meeting and raised concerns about traffic. "Nobody's thought this out. You're going to have massive traffic jams. Nobody's going to be able to get on the island, off the island," Fein said. City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved. "The city does not have a play here. We do not have a position in this. This is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. The city has been eliminated from the process," Broderick said. City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 win over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a play by teenager Lamine Yamal, and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain advanced to its first World Cup .
cards.body:
Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a heady play by teenager Lamine Yamal, Pedro Porro added another goal and Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area in the 22nd minute. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's penalty kick marked his fifth goal of this year's World Cup and the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament. It was his 30th goal in 60 international games for Spain. Porro's give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute put Spain up 2-0. Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's goal.

Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. They face each other on Wednesday in Atlanta. Kylian Mbappé and France, FIFA's top-ranked team, were trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. They instead will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday, the day before the final at MetLife Stadium. This win marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match. Yamal scored in a 2-1 win in the 2024 European Championship semifinals, and Spain won 5-4 in Nations League play last year.

cards.headline: Police investigate death of South Africa World Cup player Jayden Adams in Cape Town
cards.teaser: Police are investigating the death of 25-year-old South Africa World Cup soccer player Jayden Adams after his body was discovered Saturday at a property in Cape Town.
cards.body:
Cape Town central police registered an inquest for investigation following the discovery of the body of a 25-year-old male on Saturday, police said in a statement sent to The Associated Press. The body was discovered at a property in the Cape Town neighborhood of Schotsche Kloof at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. Authorities have not released a cause of death, and circumstances surrounding this incident are under investigation.

Adams died two weeks after helping South Africa reach the knockout stage of a World Cup for the first time. He played in all three of South Africa's group games but did not feature in the 1-0 loss to Canada in the round of 32 on June 28. South Africa Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said Adams had played in his team's group game against Czech Republic hours after learning that his grandmother had died. Adams' father, Juanito Adams, told South African TV news station eNCA on Sunday that the family were waiting for the results of an autopsy and had not yet made any funeral plans. McKenzie asked the public and media to exercise restraint and compassion and not speculate on the cause of Adams' death while authorities conduct an investigation. There were moments of silence and tributes for Adams at the England vs. Switzerland World Cup quarterfinal games on Saturday.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner wins second consecutive Wimbledon title with victory over Alexander Zverev
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his second consecutive title at the All England Club and fifth Grand Slam title.
cards.body:
Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 Sunday for his second consecutive title at the All England Club and his fifth Grand Slam title. The Italian's victory came in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, he dropped to the grass on his back in celebration. A year ago, Sinner beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final at the All England Club after wasting three match points against his rival in the Roland Garros final.

Zverev appeared bothered by a knee issue following a slip to the grass on a key point in the third set. At 3-3 in the third set, 2 hours and 42 minutes into the match, Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Zverev quickly resumed playing but appeared slightly hampered and slung his racket across the baseline in frustration when he missed a forehand and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third. It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Despite the defeat, Zverev will leapfrog Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday.

cards.headline: World Cup final four features top-ranked teams after weekend quarterfinals
cards.teaser: England and Argentina advanced to the semifinals after quarterfinal victories over Norway and Switzerland, joining Spain and France in the final four.
cards.body:
England advanced to the semifinals after Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway in the quarterfinals over the weekend. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition for England. Argentina also moved through to the last four after striker Julián Álvarez scored in extra time to help the team through to the semifinal at the expense of Switzerland, with a little help from a controversial VAR call. The semifinals now feature the four highest-ranked teams in the competition.

England is looking for its first World Cup title since 1966 and was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018, when it lost to Croatia. The team has relied on Kane and Bellingham to produce match-winning moments despite looking disjointed and vulnerable at the back. Argentina is the defending champion and has scored the most goals out of anyone in the competition with 17. Many members of the current squad won the title back in 2022. France is considered by many to be the tournament favorite, with Kylian Mbappé proving highly effective with his pace and directness. Legendary manager Didier Deschamps is leaving his role after this tournament. Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament and beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024 and in the Nations League last year.

hero.headline: Man Killed Fleeing ICE Agents on Florida Highway as Agency Faces Scrutiny Over Fatal Encounters
hero.body:
A 28-year-old man died Tuesday after he was struck by a semi trailer truck while fleeing from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents on State Road 16 near a gas station in Florida. The man was one of four people who fled on foot during an encounter with ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents in the parking lot of a local gas station and convenience store. Florida Highway Patrol officials confirmed they were not involved in the incident but have opened an investigation into the death. According to the state highway patrol, the man ran across State Road 16 and into the path of the tractor trailer. He was struck in the right lane and sustained fatal injuries on scene.

Details about the victim, including his name, nationality and immigration status, were not immediately available. ICE and the Department of Homeland Security have not yet commented on the incident. The state highway patrol said in a statement to Scripps News that during the encounter, four occupants of a vehicle fled on foot, with one running across the highway and into the path of the oncoming truck.

The death comes as ICE is under increasing scrutiny for multiple fatal encounters nationwide. Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old Colombian man living in Maine, was fatally shot by ICE agents Monday during a traffic stop. Senator Angus King said Guerrero was not the target of an immigration operation. Days earlier, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was fatally wounded during a traffic stop involving ICE in Houston. Like the shooting in Maine, Salgado Araujo was not the person ICE was trying to find.

The Trump administration ordered Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to pause most traffic stops on Tuesday following the fatal incidents. Florida Highway Patrol officials have confirmed their investigation into the State Road 16 death remains ongoing. The incident marks the latest in a series of deadly encounters involving ICE agents that have drawn attention to the agency's enforcement tactics. The pause on traffic stops comes as federal immigration enforcement operations continue under increased public and political scrutiny.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap with nine road widening projects unfunded
hero.teaser: Martin County will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years but only $701 million is currently available, leaving nine identified road widening projects without funding.
hero.body:
Martin County faces a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next two decades, with nine road widening projects left without financial backing, according to a PowerPoint obtained through a public records request. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements over the next 20 years, but only $701 million is currently available. This means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified transportation needs.

Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said the cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August. Of the $701 million currently available, all but $10 million comes from state and federal funding sources. The significant funding gap has forced difficult decisions about which transportation projects can move forward and which must remain on hold.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708.

State Road 710 is among the county's highest priorities due to safety concerns. Beltran said fatal crashes as well as serious injury crashes were just enormous on that corridor, with improvements estimated at about $300 million. The substantial price tag for State Road 710 alone represents nearly half of the total funding shortfall and highlights the challenge facing county officials as they balance safety needs against available resources. The funding gap affects not just road widening projects but a range of transportation improvements needed across the county over the next two decades.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers visitors a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, a red brick tower constructed in 1860 at the base of the Jupiter Inlet on Florida's Atlantic coast, has operated continuously for 165 years as both an active navigational aid and a public attraction. The historic structure has guided mariners since before the Civil War while welcoming visitors who make the 105-step climb to its observation gallery. The spiral staircase winds through the interior of the brick tower, following the same narrow path that lighthouse keepers climbed night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that projected light across the water to passing ships. This climb provides visitors with a tangible connection to the daily work of the keepers who ensured the beacon remained operational throughout more than a century and a half of continuous service.

The observation gallery at the top delivers panoramic views stretching across multiple waterways and the ocean. The Atlantic Ocean extends to the east, while below the tower, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet converge with the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Visitors at this elevated vantage point can watch boats glide through the channel as sea breezes sweep across the observation area. The commanding perspective reveals why this location proved ideal for a lighthouse, offering clear sightlines across the coastal landscape and waterways that allowed keepers to monitor maritime traffic and project the beacon across miles of ocean.

The museum grounds preserve more than just the tower itself. Restored historic buildings chronicle the lighthouse's journey from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. These structures provide information about the lighthouse's role in regional maritime history and offer details about the daily lives of the keepers who operated the station. The site maintains the supporting buildings that allowed the lighthouse station to function across generations.

The preservation efforts tell the complete story of this working navigational aid that has marked the Florida coastline for mariners throughout its 165 years of operation. Modern visitors follow the same path that lighthouse keepers took throughout history to maintain operations, retracing the steps of the early keepers as they ascend the narrow spiral staircase. The combination of the functioning lighthouse, restored keeper buildings, and access to the observation gallery allows visitors to experience both the historical significance and the practical purpose of this enduring coastal landmark.
